title: Split-level duplex conversion
source: Existing and demolition plans for the basement, ground floor and first floor (3/16 inch = 1 foot), the site plan and the owner's marked-up conversion sketches.

openings.tag: stair down to the ground floor

gableRoof.note: Not drawn in elevation: the planes follow the roof outline on the site plan (an east-west gable over the two-story block, a north-south gable with a Dutch gable end over the ground floor block) at an assumed 5:12 pitch.

stages.label: House
stages.line: A split-level duplex: a two-story block with a basement under a first floor unit, and a one-story ground floor wing half a level between them. Choose Explore to turn the model or go to a room.

stages.label: Street side
stages.line: The street side: the ground floor wing with its windows and the two entries the conversion sketch marks for unit 1, one on each side, with the entry landing on the east.

stages.label: Roofs
stages.line: The roofs lift away. The sheets have no roof plan or elevations, so the roof follows the outline on the site plan at an assumed pitch: a gable over the two-story block and a gable with a Dutch gable end over the ground floor wing.

stages.label: First floor
stages.line: The first floor, unit 2 today: an open kitchen, dining area and living room, a bath, a bedroom and a column of closets. Its stair down to the ground floor is the one the conversion opens to join the two units.

stages.label: Ground floor
stages.line: The ground floor of unit 1: kitchen, breakfast nook and a large living room, with a stair up to the first floor and a stair down to the basement, half a level each way.

stages.label: Basement
stages.line: The basement as it stands: a foyer from the outside stair, a master bedroom, two bedrooms, a bathroom and the hall at the foot of the stair. Both basement options on the sheets are crossed out, so it is shown unchanged.

sheetLabel: Static plan of the ground floor of a split-level duplex.
